newsitem.title: UK: UK's Norwich says no extra shares for directors.
newsitem.headline: UK's Norwich says no extra shares for directors.

text.p: Mutual insurer Norwich Union said on Wednesday that its directors would not receive any extra shares in the planned flotation of the company next summer.

In a move aimed at heading off any suggestion that the directors may have opted for demutualisation in their own interests, chief executive Allan Bridgewater said they would not be entitled to any additional shares.

"The board took this decision because we are concerned to avoid any idea that directors will benefit," he told a news conference after Norwich Union announced that it was going for a stock market listing.
However, directors will be entitled to shares in respect of any Norwich Union policies they hold.

They will also be able to buy shares in the company and both Bridgewater and chairman George Paul said they would be doing so, while finance director Richard Harvey said he could see no reason why he would not.
Bridgewater and his colleagues refused to comment on reports that the likely value of the group on flotation will be between 4.0 and 4.5 billion stg.
"That will depend on the valuation the market puts on the company as a whole," Harvey said.
Nor would they comment on media speculation that the value of free shares most policyholders will receive on flotation will be in the region of 500-700 stg.
The move to becoming a public listed company would not have any impact on staff levels or on the running of the company, Bridgewater said.

"I genuinely believe that our operations will stand institutional investigation and enquiry," he said, adding that over the last five to six years Norwich Union had been operating as if it was a quoted company.
